subject: PayGrid - model fit / eval follow-up
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Weiss <jordan.weiss@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: PayGrid - model fit / eval follow-up

Jordan - thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the next steps we discussed:

- Goals: improve invoice parsing accuracy and reduce manual review for outlier invoices (~30% of cases today).
- Success criteria (high level): reach parity with your current proprietary model for intent/slot extraction while lowering token cost by >=20% or improving latency at p95.
- Data: you confirmed we can use a de-identified sample set of ~2.5k invoices.

Recommended immediate plan:
1) Redwood will run a model-fit eval using both an open model variant (recommended: redwood/open-7b-quant) and your proprietary baseline (we'll treat it as the reference).
2) We'll evaluate on the same prompt set and metrics (intent_f1, slot_f1, hallucination rate, latency_p95, token_cost_per_1k).
3) Deliverable: a one-page parity report + detailed benchmark CSV + suggested prompt adjustments and quantization profile.

Attachments: paygrid_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (prompt/test pairs), and a recent benchmark summary for a comparable customer (paygrid_benchmark_report_q2.pdf).

Ask from you: please share the de-identified sample dataset and confirm any intents/slots that are considered "critical" (we'll prioritize those in the regression checks).

Proposed timeline: we can run an initial parity eval within ~5 business days after we have the sample data. Would you be available for a 30-min follow-up the week of 5/12 to review results?

Thanks - looking forward to moving this forward.

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Jordan Weiss <jordan.weiss@paygrid.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PayGrid - model fit / eval follow-up

Lauren - really appreciate the summary and the clear plan. A couple quick clarifications before we hand over data:

1) Parity thresholds - can you propose concrete acceptance thresholds for the eval? Our internal bar for replacing the baseline is fairly high on a couple of critical intents.
2) Latency/cost targets - what p95 latency and token-cost numbers should we expect for the open model config you recommended?
3) Data delivery - we'll share the de-identified set (2.5k rows) early tomorrow. Any preferred format aside from the prompt set you attached?

If you can include recommended thresholds in your next note that would help align our stakeholders. 30-min the week of 5/12 works - prefer 5/13 or 5/14 mornings.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Weiss
Head of ML Ops | PayGrid
jordan.weiss@paygrid.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Weiss <jordan.weiss@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 08:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PayGrid - model fit / eval follow-up

On Thu, May 6, 2027 at 8:17 AM Jordan Weiss <jordan.weiss@paygrid.com> wrote:
> Lauren - really appreciate the summary and the clear plan. A couple quick clarifications before we hand over data:
>
> 1) Parity thresholds - can you propose concrete acceptance thresholds for the eval? Our internal bar for replacing the baseline is fairly high on a couple of critical intents.
> 2) Latency/cost targets - what p95 latency and token-cost numbers should we expect for the open model config you recommended?
> 3) Data delivery - we'll share the de-identified set (2.5k rows) early tomorrow. Any preferred format aside from the prompt set you attached?

Thanks for the questions - below are the concrete thresholds and what we'll measure in the parity eval:

Suggested acceptance thresholds (initial):
- intent_f1 >= 0.95 relative to proprietary baseline (measured as F1 ratio >= 0.95 on critical intents)
- slot_f1 within 0.03 absolute points of baseline on extraction slots deemed critical
- hallucination_rate no more than 2% absolute increase vs baseline on critical extraction tasks
- latency_p95: target < 350ms for the redwood/open-7b-quant profile (hosted/dedicated config)
- token_cost_per_1k: target <= 0.80x of baseline cost (we'll report tokenized unit economics per 1k tokens)

Notes:
- These thresholds are intentionally conservative for the first pass - if we see systematic gaps on specific intents we will propose targeted prompt patches, quantization profiles, or a slightly larger model variant (open-13b-quant) to hit parity.
- For latency we will measure both cold and warm KV-cache runs and report p50/p95.

Preferred data format: CSV (rows of de-identified invoice text + metadata columns). The prompt/test pairs you attached are ideal for prompt parity; if you send raw text we will synthesize the prompt pairs on our side using the attached prompt set.

Timeline & next steps:
- You share data tomorrow -> we start eval within 24 hours -> preliminary parity report in ~5 business days.
- Schedule 30-min results review (5/13 or 5/14). Please tell me which time you prefer.

I'll loop Marissa and Aditya internally to run the benchmark and produce the deliverables.

-Lauren

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: FW: PayGrid - model fit / eval follow-up

Marissa / Aditya - forwarding Jordan's note and our plan. Can you run the parity eval once PayGrid shares the de-identified CSV? Key asks below:

Scope: run parity eval comparing:
- redwood/open-7b-quant (primary open candidate)
- redwood/open-13b-quant (only if 7b misses critical intents by >0.05)
- paygrid_proprietary_baseline (their reference)

Metrics to produce (same CSV output format as our standard eval harness):
- intent_f1 (overall + per-critical-intent)
- slot_f1 (overall + per-slot)
- hallucination_rate (instances where model invents fields)
- latency_p50, latency_p95 (cold vs warm cache)
- token_cost_per_1k (cost model matching our hosted pricing)

Acceptance thresholds to check:
- intent_f1 >= 0.95 of baseline on critical intents
- slot_f1 within 0.03 absolute points on critical slots
- hallucination_rate no more than +2% absolute vs baseline
- latency_p95 < 350ms (for 7b config)
- token_cost_per_1k <= 0.80x baseline

Resources/inputs: paygrid_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (attached), paygrid_sample_data_v2.csv (will be uploaded to Drive - link is in the thread metadata), PG-3921 HubSpot deal id (use for naming conventions).

Deliverables: parity_report_onepage.pdf, benchmark_details_PG-3921.csv, raw_eval_logs.tar.gz. Preliminary results by EOD 2027-05-12 if data arrives tomorrow.

Notes / caveats: if the open-7b-quant shows targeted regressions on a small set of intents we should include a short list of prompt adjustments and a recompute step rather than immediately recommending 13b. Also capture examples of hallucinations with context for the CS/MLOps team.

Thanks - please confirm receipt and estimated ETA.

-Lauren
